html:
Ribe, on the west coast of Jutland, is the oldest town in Scandinavia. A seasonal market there began in the early 700s, before the Viking Age.

Traders from Frisia and the Frankish lands came to exchange glass, wine and pottery for slaves, furs and cattle. Craftsmen made beads and combs on the spot. Ribe was linked by sea to the other great Danish market at Hedeby.

The missionary Ansgar was allowed to build a church in Ribe about 860, one of the first in Denmark, and it became a bishop's seat in the next century. The cathedral and the old streets survive. Ribe stayed an important port until its harbour silted up and trade shifted to the east coast.
sum: Ribe, on the west coast of Jutland, is the oldest town in Scandinavia. A seasonal market there began in the early 700s, before the Viking Age.
